correctness.rationale: For each nonempty frequency, the connected-set indicator splits into the constant function minus the empty atom and the disjoint within-part non-singleton supports. Explicit elementary character sums yield every integer Walsh multiplier. Parity and a constructed zero frequency give both sides of invertibility; a constructed unit multiplier proves sharp conditioning; a disjoint omitted-part partition proves nullity; Stirling proves the limiting density. The checked standalone exact transform agreed with predictions for 136 complete multipartite shapes (751 assertions); tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: This gives a complete natural recovery classification across arbitrary multipartite part sizes: a parity switch between no information loss and an explicitly structured kernel. It includes the exact entire eigenvalue formula, a finite coefficient formula for all lost frequencies, a sharp invertible condition number and a universal Gaussian-scale loss in large balanced shapes. The structural fact is not just the classical connected-subset count; it identifies which Fourier information is recoverable and why. The data are graph-combinatorial and Fourier-analytic without arbitrary parameter slices.
